contextModules.title: Hierarchy and brand
contextModules.summary: Establish user priority, information hierarchy, brand expression, and token-driven composition before decoration.

contextModules.title: Visual composition and polish
contextModules.summary: Apply disciplined type scale, spacing rhythm, alignment, surface hierarchy, density, component defaults, scroll ownership, and rendered visual review.

contextModules.title: Responsive behavior and complete states
contextModules.summary: Adapt interaction and information hierarchy by content constraints while proving loading, empty, error, permission, success, and recovery states.

contextModules.title: React boundaries
contextModules.summary: Keep client rendering narrow when the bound project uses React or a compatible server-rendering model.

contextModules.title: Human interface writing
contextModules.summary: Write focused, plain, useful product language that supports decisions, actions, understanding, recovery, inclusion, and user agency.

contextModules.title: Component architecture and naming
contextModules.summary: Prevent duplicate components and prompt-shaped APIs by making reuse decisions and naming durable semantic responsibilities.

contextModules.title: Anti-slop visual review
contextModules.summary: Review rendered evidence for generic visual treatment, repeated copy, token drift, missing states, overflow, and weak interaction hierarchy.

failureSignals.summary: Raw color, spacing, radius, or shadow values recur where project tokens exist.
Small interactive behavior repeatedly expands the client-rendered component tree.
Interfaces repeatedly expose technical terms, duplicate headings, vague actions, robotic language, dead ends, or unnecessary explanatory text.
Desktop layouts repeatedly compress or overflow instead of adapting to content and interaction constraints.
Type roles, spacing rhythm, alignment, or density repeatedly obscure the page's primary reading order.
Nested cards, borders, shadows, pills, or competing surfaces repeatedly replace whitespace and hierarchy.
Bounded content, scrolling, navigation state, focus, or persistent controls repeatedly fail in the rendered interface.
Agents repeatedly create components, wrappers, or variants that duplicate an existing semantic role or extension point.
Component, prop, or variant names repeatedly mirror temporary request wording, visual treatment, motion, or feature-local adjectives instead of durable roles.
Shell, breadcrumb, eyebrow, title, description, navigation, and panel copy repeatedly compete for the same language role.

adaptationQuestions: Which project sources own brand doctrine, tokens, and component behavior?
Which catalog, exports, symbol search, and naming rules define reusable component ownership?
Which rendered screens are explicitly approved precedents, and why?
Which actions produce responsive and accessibility evidence?
Which terms are preferred or prohibited in customer-facing interfaces?
Who is the audience, what knowledge can be assumed, and which voice and tone rules are accepted?
Which actions are destructive, regulated, privacy-sensitive, or required to remain reversible?
Which semantic type, spacing, surface, border, radius, and elevation roles are canonical?
Which shell regions own scrolling, persistent controls, route state, and responsive adaptation?
